'''Kamo no Tadayuki''' (賀茂 忠行) was a {{ill|Nobility|en|Nobility|qid=Q134737|lt=noble}} and {{ill|School of Naturalists|en|School of Naturalists|qid=Q1195540|lt=Onmyōji}} active during the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Early Heian period}} to {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Mid Heian period}}. He is best known as the mentor of {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|Abe no Seimei|qid=Q1150151|lt=Abe no Seimei}}. His father was either {{ill|Kamo no Enjin|ja|賀茂江人}} or {{ill|Kamo no Mineo|ja|賀茂峯雄}}. He held the court Rank of Junior Fifth Rank and served as Assistant Governor of Tanba.

== Achievements ==

Kamo no Tadayuki excelled in the art of {{ill|Onmyōdō|en|Onmyōdō|qid=Q1340540|lt=divination}}, earning unwavering trust from the {{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|qid=Q208233|lt=Emperor of Japan}}. He was particularly renowned for his skill in ''{{ill|Shikuku|ja|射覆}}'' (divining the contents of a concealed object). One notable incident, recorded in the {{ill|Konjaku Monogatarishū|en|Konjaku Monogatarishū|qid=Q1507085|lt=Konjaku Monogatari}}, describes how he correctly identified a crystal rosary wrapped in red cord hidden in an octagonal box, astonishing the emperor and earning widespread acclaim.

== Role in Onmyōdō History ==

Tadayuki's contributions to {{ill|Onmyōdō|en|Onmyōdō|qid=Q1340540|lt=Onmyōdō}} were pivotal. Prior to his time, the three branches of Onmyōdō—{{ill|Astronomy|ja|天文道|lt=Tenmondō}}, {{ill|Calendar-making|ja|暦道}}, and {{ill|Onmyōdō|en|Onmyōdō|qid=Q1340540|lt=Onmyōdō proper}}—were practiced separately by specialized experts. However, Tadayuki, originally a {{ill|Rekidō|ja|暦家|lt=Calendar scholar}}, transcended these divisions, uniting the disciplines under the leadership of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂氏}}. This consolidation laid the groundwork for the future dominance of the Kamo and {{ill|Abe clan|ja|安倍氏|zh|安倍氏|qid=Q10946389}} in Onmyōdō.

== Historical Context ==

The suspension of the {{ill|Japanese missions to Tang China|fa|هیئت‌های اعزامی ژاپنی به تانگ چین|fr|Missions japonaises dans la Chine des Tang|id|Misi Jepang ke Tang Tiongkok|it|Missioni giapponesi nella Cina Tang|ja|遣唐使|ko|견당사|zh|遣唐使|zh_min_nan|Khián Tông sú|qid=Q262529|lt=Kentōshi}} missions in the 6th year of Kanpyō (894) under {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ar|سوغاوارا نو ميتشيزانه|br|Sugawara no Michizane|ckb|سوگاوارا نۆ میچیزانێ|de|Sugawara no Michizane|es|Sugawara no Michizane|fa|سوگاوارا نو میچی‌زانه|fi|Sugawara no Michizane|fr|Sugawara no Michizane|id|Sugawara no Michizane|it|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真|kk|Сугавара но Митидзане|ko|스가와라노 미치자네|la|Sugawara no Michizane|ms|Sugawara no Michizane|nl|Sugawara no Michizane|nn|Sugawara no Michizane|pl|Michizane Sugawara|pt|Sugawara no Michizane|ru|Сугавара-но Митидзанэ|sh|Sugawara no Michizane|sv|Sugawara no Michizane|th|สึกาวาระ โนะ มิจิซาเนะ|tr|Sugawara no Michizane|uk|Суґавара но Мітідзане|zh|菅原道真|zh_classical|菅原道真|zh_min_nan|Sugawara no Mitizane|qid=Q382005}} meant that no new knowledge on {{ill|Yin-Yang and Wuxing Theory|ja|陰陽五行思想|ko|음양오행설|qid=Q11265234}} was being imported from the continent. This restriction fostered an environment where Onmyōdō practices became increasingly reliant on existing knowledge. The Kamo clan took advantage of this situation to innovate, blending {{ill|Taoism|af|Taoïsme|als|Daoismus|an|Taoísmo|anp|ताओ == Appearances in Literature and Media ==

Tadayuki is featured prominently in legends such as:
* ''Konjaku Monogatari'': Narratives detail his encounters with {{ill|Hyakki Yagyō|ar|الموكب الليلي للمئة شيطان|ca|Hyakki Yako|cdo|百鬼夜行|ckb|ھیاکی یاگیۆ|el|Χιάκι Γιακό|es|Hyakki Yagyō|fr|Hyakki yakō|hy|Հյակկի Յագյո|it|Hyakki yagyō|ja|百鬼夜行|ko|백귀야행|pl|Hyakki-yakō|ru|Хякки яко|zh|百鬼夜行|qid=Q1358278|lt=Hyakki Yagyō}} and his mentorship of Abe no Seimei.
* He is depicted in modern adaptations such as:
** ''{{ill|Q11658268|ja|陰陽師☆安倍晴明〜王都妖奇譚〜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōji☆Abe Seimei: Royal Capital Mystical Tales|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11658268}}'' (2002, Fuji TV), played by {{ill|Yasutaka Tsutsui|en|Yasutaka Tsutsui|qid=Q719250|lt=Yasutaka Tsutsui}}.
** ''{{ill|Q24873669|ja|ねこねこ日本史|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Neko Neko Nihonshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q24873669}}'' (2018, NHK), voiced by {{ill|Yusuke Shirai|en|Yusuke Shirai|qid=Q11579372|lt=Yūsuke Shirai}}.
